empty.pcap.explanation: The analyzer requires a complete classic pcap header; TShark 4.2.2 accepts this zero-byte file as zero frames.

tshark.stderr: tshark: The file "<fixture>" appears to have been cut short in the middle of a packet.

record_cutoff.pcap.explanation: Both reject an incomplete record body. The analyzer identifies the body boundary and planned packet index; neither counts the partial body as a frame.

tshark.stderr: tshark: The file "<fixture>" appears to have been cut short in the middle of a packet.

header_cutoff.pcap.explanation: Both reject an incomplete record header. The analyzer distinguishes it from a short body; TShark uses the same cut-short diagnostic for both.

malformed_length.pcap.explanation: Both read the complete record and preserve caplen 55 and wirelen 54. The analyzer classifies the contradiction as malformed and excludes it from flows; TShark still extracts TCP fields. Exit 0 does not imply a valid packet.

unsupported_linktype.pcap.explanation: The analyzer accepts only Ethernet link type 1; TShark accepts this raw-IP link type 101 header with zero frames. This does not verify raw-IP packet decoding.

unsupported_pcapng.pcapng.explanation: The analyzer explicitly rejects pcapng; TShark accepts this section-header-only pcapng with zero frames. No interface or packet blocks are present.
